method.derivation: Every field except per-name `kind`/`rationale` is derived from the manifests, pnpm-lock.yaml importers/catalogs blocks, installed package metadata and a line-anchored source scan.
method.annotations: `kind` and `rationale` are hand-verified per EXTERNAL name (no file records intent). A declared external dependency without an annotation fails --check.
method.useSites: file/line/via/symbols evidence from import, dynamic import, require, require.resolve, tsconfig types, config strings and package scripts. Not an AST.

kinds.runtime: shipped code the product executes (browser, worker or CLI runtime)
kinds.test: only test suites, test runners, coverage or fixtures use it
kinds.type-only: TypeScript declarations only; contributes no runtime code
kinds.config: consumed by a build/lint/format configuration file or a tool configuration string; not shipped
kinds.bin: invoked as an executable by package scripts or CI
kinds.workspace: internal @assay package link, not a third-party dependency

limits: Literal, line-anchored use-site evidence only: a dependency consumed implicitly has no site and says so in its annotation instead of inventing one.
At most 10 use sites are stored per entry; useSiteCount stays exact, so a change beyond the stored head is caught by the count rather than the list.
Only direct declarations are listed; transitive packages are out of scope.
engines/peerDependencies are read from the installed package metadata, not from the registry.
Engine and peer ranges are recorded as data; range compatibility is not decided here.

engines/peerDependencies come from the installed packages, so a lock that resolves platform-specific optional dependencies can legitimately change them; --check reports that as metadata drift instead of passing silently.
Installed byte sizes live in the measurements report, never here: install size is not bundle weight.

reviewConclusion.claim: The accepted 31-name dependency review found no verified behaviour-equivalent built-in module or <20-line replacement for any external direct dependency.
reviewConclusion.evidence: 31 external direct names, no name reached the "equivalence proven" verdict; every name is annotated `none proven` with its observed API surface and use sites. This manifest does not remove or upgrade any dependency; see the removal policy in docs/engineering/10-dependency-and-bundle-measurements.md §10.

annotations.name: @axe-core/playwright
annotations.rationale: axe-core rule engine injected into Playwright pages for the e2e accessibility gate (tests/e2e/support/a11y.ts); the gate asserts on axe's violation model, and no built-in or small replacement provides the rule engine plus that model.

annotations.name: @changesets/cli
annotations.rationale: release/changeset tooling invoked by `pnpm changeset`; AGENTS.md requires a changeset with package changes, and the config in .changeset/ is read only by this binary.
annotations.notes: The package is not a runtime dependency of any shipped artifact.

annotations.name: @duckdb/duckdb-wasm
annotations.rationale: the browser analytical engine: DuckDB-WASM runs in a Web Worker and serves every SQL, Parquet, CSV and profile path. The desktop build copies its `eh` wasm/worker from the lockfile-pinned package, so the resolved version is part of the product bytes.
annotations.pinRationale: declared `^1.32.0` and locked to 1.32.0. ADR 0048 and apps/vscode/assets/duckdb/VENDORED_ASSETS.md pin the wasm/worker by SHA-256 and verify byte-equality against this installed package on every build, so a bump requires re-vendoring, pin regeneration and cross-surface agreement — never a latest-tag bump.
annotations.notes: Install size (144 MB) is the published package on disk, not the shipped bundle: the browser app loads one wasm/worker pair lazily (see the measurement report).

annotations.name: @duckdb/node-api
annotations.rationale: the CLI's native DuckDB engine (apps/cli/src/connection.ts and the node executor): CLI inspection, SQL, diff and export execute through it.
annotations.pinRationale: exact `1.5.5-r.5`, tracking the DuckDB CLI v1.5.5 that fixtures/parquet/generate.sh and the parity scripts use (ADR 0038/0041). Platform bindings (`@duckdb/node-bindings-*`) arrive as optional transitive binaries, so the lock is platform-dependent; a bump must move the API and the CLI together.
annotations.notes: Native binary package: install size includes the linux-x64 binding, not portable byte counts.

annotations.name: @eslint/js
annotations.rationale: flat-config `js.configs.recommended` preset imported by eslint.config.js; the lint gate depends on it.
annotations.notes: Declared `^9.30.0` and locked to 9.39.5 beside eslint 10.11.0 — two version facts, no compatibility inference.

annotations.name: @playwright/test
annotations.rationale: browser e2e runner for tests/e2e/** (the only browser-suite entry point) and the CI workflow's browser install step; the harnesses under packages/{engine-duckdb,data-sources}/harness exist for this suite.

annotations.name: @tanstack/react-virtual
annotations.rationale: headless row virtualization for the grid viewport: windowed rendering, scroll-to-index and range math for the >1M-row path. No built-in browser API provides windowed rendering.

annotations.name: @testing-library/react
annotations.rationale: component tests for apps/web (queried the way a user would) under the happy-dom environment; test-only.

annotations.name: @types/node
annotations.rationale: ambient Node typings: the tsconfig `types` entries (root, packages, apps/vscode/test) and every `node:*` import typecheck against it. No runtime code is emitted.
annotations.notes: Seven workspaces declare it. packages/telemetry declares it for the Web-standard globals it provides under `lib: ES2022` only (no DOM lib) — the tsconfig `types` entry is the recorded site.

annotations.name: @types/react
annotations.rationale: React/JSX typings that tsc resolves for every `react` import in apps/web; TypeScript has no built-in JSX library typing. Compile time only.
annotations.notes: Consumed implicitly through TypeScript's module resolution for every `react` import: the recorded sites are those imports (`via: module-types`), not a literal `@types/react` specifier.

annotations.name: @types/react-dom
annotations.rationale: typings for react-dom and the client entry used by apps/web; compile time only.
annotations.notes: Consumed implicitly, like @types/react; declared for the react-dom surface.

annotations.name: @types/vscode
annotations.rationale: VS Code extension-host API typings for apps/vscode (activation, custom editor, webview API); compile time only.
annotations.pinRationale: `^1.90.0` matches the manifest's `engines.vscode` floor, so the typings cannot promise an API newer than the declared host floor.

annotations.name: @vitejs/plugin-react
annotations.rationale: React JSX transform and Fast Refresh for the Vite web build (apps/web/vite.config.ts); build-time only.

annotations.name: @vitest/coverage-v8
annotations.rationale: V8 coverage provider named in vitest.config.ts; the coverage thresholds in that config are enforced through it.

annotations.name: @vscode/test-electron
annotations.rationale: runs the desktop runtime suite in a real VS Code build (apps/vscode/scripts/run-e2e.mjs); test-only and never part of the extension payload.
annotations.notes: Needs an offline VS Code cache or a provision run; the doctor script reports it as an optional prerequisite.

annotations.name: apache-arrow
annotations.rationale: Arrow is the interchange format between the engine, the CLI and the test fixtures (tables cross the worker boundary and the CLI's node seam as Arrow vectors). No built-in replacement exists for the Arrow IPC/table model.
annotations.pinRationale: exact `17.0.0` so the JS Arrow version matches the DuckDB-WASM client's declared arrow peer; a bump has to move the engine and the CLI together.

annotations.name: esbuild
annotations.rationale: bundles the VS Code extension host and webview entries in apps/vscode/scripts/build.mjs (imported as a JS API, not only as a binary); the desktop payload on every native dependency graph is produced by it.
annotations.notes: Also recorded as a `bin` because the build script calls its JS API; there is no built-in bundler for .cjs extension output.

entries.name: @duckdb/duckdb-wasm
entries.rationale: the browser analytical engine: DuckDB-WASM runs in a Web Worker and serves every SQL, Parquet, CSV and profile path. The desktop build copies its `eh` wasm/worker from the lockfile-pinned package, so the resolved version is part of the product bytes.
entries.pinRationale: declared `^1.32.0` and locked to 1.32.0. ADR 0048 and apps/vscode/assets/duckdb/VENDORED_ASSETS.md pin the wasm/worker by SHA-256 and verify byte-equality against this installed package on every build, so a bump requires re-vendoring, pin regeneration and cross-surface agreement — never a latest-tag bump.

entries.name: @duckdb/node-api
entries.rationale: the CLI's native DuckDB engine (apps/cli/src/connection.ts and the node executor): CLI inspection, SQL, diff and export execute through it.
entries.pinRationale: exact `1.5.5-r.5`, tracking the DuckDB CLI v1.5.5 that fixtures/parquet/generate.sh and the parity scripts use (ADR 0038/0041). Platform bindings (`@duckdb/node-bindings-*`) arrive as optional transitive binaries, so the lock is platform-dependent; a bump must move the API and the CLI together.

entries.name: apache-arrow
entries.rationale: Arrow is the interchange format between the engine, the CLI and the test fixtures (tables cross the worker boundary and the CLI's node seam as Arrow vectors). No built-in replacement exists for the Arrow IPC/table model.
entries.pinRationale: exact `17.0.0` so the JS Arrow version matches the DuckDB-WASM client's declared arrow peer; a bump has to move the engine and the CLI together.
